condition.narrative: Section I.A.1 (a): Establish, not later than three months after the Effective Date, and thereafter maintain throughout Programimplementation, a strategic working group for the support of the implementation of the Program (“Steering Committee”), comprised ofrepresentatives of each Implementing Institution, responsible for strategic oversight and guidance under the Program, all underterms and conditions acceptable to the Bank

Section I.A.1 (b): Ensure that each Implementing Institution will appoint, by not later than three months from the Date ofEffectiveness, the focal points under terms satisfactory to the Bank, to monitor and oversee the implementation of the Program,including social and environmental requirements of the Program, if applicable; as well as provide inputs for the Program reportsnot later than 30 days after the end of each calendar semester.Section I.A.1 (c): Ensure that the MoH and Other ImplementingInstitutions shall maintain, throughout the implementation of the Program, the functions, staffing and resources appropriate tofulfill their respective functions under the Program (including technical, social and environmental safeguards, monitoring andfiduciary functions).Section I.A.1 (d): Carry out, through the MoH, the monitoring of day-to-day implementation of the Program,consolidate the Program's progress reports, and financial statements and submit the Verification Reports to the Bank.

Section I.B of the Schedule 2: The Borrower, through the MoH and the Other Implementing Institutions, shall carry out the ProgramAction Plan, or cause the Program Action Plan to be carried out, in accordance with the schedule set out in the said Program ActionPlan in a manner satisfactory to the Bank.
Section III.A: The Borrower, through the MoH, shall furnish to the Bank each Program Report not later than forty five (45) daysafter the end of each calendar semester, covering the calendar semester.

Section III.B.1 (a): No later than four months after the Effective Date, or such later date as agreed by the Bank, appoint/selectand thereafter maintain, throughout the implementation of the Program, one or more independent verification agents, as needed, withqualifications and experience and under term of reference acceptable to the Bank to verify the data and other evidence supportingthe achievement of one or more DLIs/DLRs.Section III.B.1 (b): (i) ensure that each Independent Verification Agent carry outverification and processes in accordance with the Verification Protocol; and (ii) submit to the Bank the corresponding verificationreports in a timely manner and in form and substance satisfactory to the Bank.

title.narrative: At least 50% of patented medicines positively assessed through the new HTA methodology receive conditional reimbursement decisions

comment.narrative: In progress. Development of the new HTA methodology is ongoing. Technical assistance is being provided to update the HTA methodology, in line with standards outlined by the NHIH and the MoH. The new methodology is expected to be completed by June 2025. Once complete, the associated legislation will be drafted and publicly consulted (October 2025), after which the legislative approval process will begin, with approval expected by November 2025 by Ministerial Order. Once the legislation is approved, reimbursement for patented medicines positively assessed should begin to increase within four months.

title.narrative: Number of community health care workers (community health nurses and Roma health mediators) trained

comment.narrative: Achieved. Training has been provided to all community health care network (1,946 community health care workers and 468 Roma mediators) on usage of the upgraded version of the AMCMSR App. Beyond this, another training course was conducted for 158 community health workers (and up to 350 community health care workers who covered personally the training fee) as part of the POCU project. A subsequent POIDS (EU/Managing Authority for the Inclusion and Social Dignity Programs) project that covers training of 2,000 community health care workers and Roma health mediators is expected to be held in July 2025. There are already 150 collaboration protocols concluded between the community health centers and PHC providers. In September 2025, it is expected that there will be 500 integrated community health care teams ready to start the work.

Progress on this indicator is expected to continue, with 2,000 integrated community health care centers supported by the Romaniaâ€™s recovery and resilience plan and 150 communities supported by the EU/Managing Authority for the Inclusion and Social Dignity Programs (POIDS) to start in July 2025.

title.narrative: Percentage of uninsured who are aware they are entitled to receive an improved PHC benefit package (aligned with the basic benefits package for the insured)

comment.narrative:
On track. Communications on the approved changes to the Health Law were developed and rolled out by the NHIH, including two rounds of communications campaigns implemented in both 2023 and 2024. Implementation is ongoing in 2025. In addition, a dedicated section of the NHIH website has been created for the uninsured.
To reach further individuals, additional communication tools will be implemented under the leadership of the MoH. Technical assistance to develop and roll out a communication strategy is expected to be signed by end May 2025.
Given that the indicator refers to the percentage of uninsured who are aware of the benefit, this indicator will be based on a research in a sample of communities (not on the entire uninsured population which would be substantially expensive to carry out).

title.narrative: Percentage of National Health Insurance Houseâ€™s annual budget allocated to PHC (Percentage, Custom)

comment.narrative: The share of the expenditure for PHC has continued to grow nominally in 2023 and 2024 (+13% y/y and +45% y/y, respectively). By 2024, the actual expenditure on PHC was 3% higher than forecast under the Programâ€™s expenditure framework. The large growth in expenditure in 2024 was due to the impact of reforms related to the scope of service packages and provider-payment mechanisms that entered into force in July 2023 and had a full year of implementation. As a result, while in 2023 the initial PHC budget was 25% higher than the executed budget, in 2024 the executed value was 43% higher than the initial budget (the executed PHC expenditure in 2024 was RON 5.3 billion or US$ 1.15 billion equivalent or 7.7% of the total National Health Insurance Fund expenditure for health services). For 2025, the initial PHC expenditure is 2.5% higher than in 2024 due to stability in the scope of the service packages and tariffs; the share in total NHIF expenditure for health services is measured at 7.6%.

comment.narrative: In progress. The Digital Health Strategy has been drafted and underwent public consultation (December 2024). The Health Data Masterplan, which is part of the overall Digital Health Strategy, is being finalized and is expected to be submitted to the MoH for approval by June 2025. The TWG, created under the WHO/RRP, was changed at the time when the strategy was to be presented to the MoH for approval. The strategy is now with the revised TWG for feedback. To support the implementation of the Digital Health Strategy, once adopted, a Digital Health Unit has been created (January 2025) and has been staffed with a Head of the Unit and one expert.
